Plotting myDAR walks

Source: vignettes/mydar-walks.Rmd
mydar-walks.Rmd

myDAR maps a site from a phone walk. Each walk produces a point cloud, a DEM, a GeoPackage with the track, GPS fixes and accuracy figures, and the device trajectory. myIO reads those files into data frames and plots them.

Reading a walk

read_mydar_walk() reads a walk output directory:

File Element Reader
walk.copc.laz points read_mydar_points() (needs rlas)
terrain.tif terrain read_mydar_terrain() (needs terra)
orthophoto.tif orthophoto read_mydar_orthophoto() (needs terra)
walk.gpkg track, track_points, gps_fixes, pins, features, accuracy read_mydar_gpkg() (needs sf)
trajectory.csv trajectory read_mydar_trajectory()

myIO does not install rlas, terra or sf; the readers ask for them when they need them.

walk <- read_mydar_walk("path/to/walk", max_points = 20000)
walk

The reader keeps max_points of the cloud (every k-th point in file order, which keeps the relative density across the walk; Inf keeps them all) and records the full count. The DEM is aggregated when it has more than max_cells cells. By default every table moves to walk-local coordinates by subtraction: x and y become meters from the walk’s south-west corner, z the height above the lowest ground cell (walk$origin holds the shift). The orthophoto comes back as a plain PNG with its extent in the same coordinates.

The examples below use mydar_iphone_walk: a real outdoor walk recorded with the myDAR iPhone app and processed with the myDAR CLI (autodar commit a1388d8), shown in local coordinates only. Its x and y were moved to meters from the walk’s south-west corner and its heights to height above the lowest ground cell, by subtraction only; the subtracted origin and the project CRS are not included, and the orthophoto ships as pixels only. Classes, point sigma, GPS residuals and the accuracy figures are as measured. It keeps 6,000 points for the SVG charts; mydar_iphone_cloud() returns 500,000 of the walk’s points for the 3D view. Neither needs the optional packages. data-raw/mydar_iphone_walk.R in the myIO repository builds both from a walk folder.

walk <- mydar_iphone_walk
walk
#> <mydar_walk>
#>   points:       6,000 of 887,038
#>   terrain:      9,783 cells
#>   track:        26 vertices
#>   gps_fixes:    49
#>   features:     none
#>   trajectory:   2,984 poses
#>   orthophoto:   352 x 453 px
#>   local coordinates (origin withheld)

A profile line across the middle of the track, used below:

ym <- mean(range(walk$track$y))
line <- list(from = c(0, ym), to = c(22, ym))

The views

3D point cloud

The cloud in 3D, the way the myDAR app’s Results screen shows it: drag to orbit, shift-drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom, or switch to 2D for a top-down plan with a scale bar. The chips color the points by camera color, class, height or sigma and turn the orthophoto under them on and off. The card gives the walk’s two accuracy figures, Shape and Map, separately.

mydar_cloud_view(walk, points = mydar_iphone_cloud())

Plan view

The orthophoto with the points (by LAS class), the track and the profile line over it, drawn to scale (setEqualAspect()), with the accuracy figures in the corner. mydar_orthophoto_view() shows the orthophoto alone.

mydar_plan_view(walk, profile = line)

Terrain

The DEM uses the raster chart type: a grid of cells drawn as one image, colored by height and shaded by a hillshade. Hover a cell for its height.

mydar_terrain_view(walk, azimuth = 315, altitude = 45)

The raster type works for any regular grid: map x_var, y_var (cell centers) and value, and optionally shade (0-1).

grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 5, by = 0.1), y = seq(0, 3, by = 0.1))
grid$value <- sin(grid$x) * cos(grid$y)
myIO() |>
  addIoLayer(type = "raster", label = "value", data = grid,
             mapping = list(x_var = "x", y_var = "y", value = "value"),
             options = list(palette = "cividis"))

Profile

Points within a corridor along a line, as height against distance along the line, with the DEM height along the same line. mydar_profile() returns the corridor points as a data frame.

mydar_profile_view(walk, from = line$from, to = line$to, width = 0.5)
head(mydar_profile(walk, from = line$from, to = line$to))

Uncertainty and QA 

mydar_trajectory_view(walk)
mydar_gps_view(walk)
mydar_sigma_view(walk)
mydar_accuracy_view(walk)

mydar_gps_view() plots each GPS fix’s residual against the fused track, next to the 95% residual the processing expected. sigma_m is the per-point 1-sigma per axis that the cloud stores, on a log10 axis because camera points (when a walk has them) run to meters while LiDAR stays near 2-3 cm; this walk is LiDAR only. The accuracy chart puts the shape figure (how well distances inside the walk hold) next to map position (where the walk sits on the map). Here the map position comes from phone GPS, so it is far larger than the shape figure within 5 m.

All at once

mydar_dashboard() lays out the views on one page in the app’s order: the 3D cloud and the plan view first, then the profile, then the quality charts. Brush the plan view and the same points light up on the profile; hover the uncertainty or GPS chart and the other shows a cursor at the same moment (the GPS chart appears when the walk has GPS residuals).

mydar_dashboard(walk, points = mydar_iphone_cloud())
